newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC approves digital radio service auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC approves digital radio service auction.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Monday approved plans for the long-awaited auction of two airwave licenses to set up a new type of radio service that promises CD-quality sound and can be heard nationwide.

The auction, to occur in April, had been delayed for years while the FCC's commissioners sought to resolve long-standing differences over how to allocate the two licenses to the four companies vying to offer digital audio radio.
The four are: CD Radio Inc ; American Mobile Radio Corp, a unit of American Mobile Satellite Corp ; Digital Broadcast Satellite Corp; and Primosphere LP.
Unlike conventional radio, the new digitally based service will offer listeners crystal-clear sound and will be broadcast coast-to-coast via satellite.
Listeners will have to buy a special radio and antenna. It is likely the service will be subscription-based.
Despite reservations from two commissioners, the agency agreed to limit the auction of the two licenses to the four companies -- which had filed applications with the FCC several years ago.

FCC Chairman Reed Hundt and Commissioner Susan Ness had favored opening the auction to all eligible bidders. But they were unable to get the other two commissioners at the FCC -- Rachelle Chong and James Quello -- to agree.
"I would prefer to assign spectrum licenses through an auction open to all. Closing the auction is the wrong result," Hundt said in a statement.
